text_fidelity_a: FiiO BTR5-384K/32Bit Native DSD256 Hi-Res CSR8675 Bluetooth5.0 Receiver/USB DAC/DSD Headphone Amp with LDAC, aptX HD, aptX, AAC (3.5mm Unbalanced&2.5mm Balanced Output, Black) Ok, it is really Bluetooth but OMG. I own a Radsone ES100, bought it when it was the new kid on the block and it is a great piece of kit. Amazing sound, unparalleled software, so-so materials and construction. But this FiiO is like the candle you burn from both ends, you know, twice the light but half the time. This thing will drive ANY IEM’s you have to ear bleeding levels and when you look you’re at 45, OUT OF 100 on the volume scale. And while I am an IEM guy I do own a pair of HiFiMan HE-400i planars and I rarely see anything above 55 on the volume with it on Hi Gain. And granted they are only 35 ohm I have it on good authority that they will drive the big boys with out breaking a sweat. The only gripe I have is the battery life. I only run 2.5mm balanced so the battery usually taps out after about 5-6 hours. Not bad, but not the ES100’s 10 hours. But the power, man this sucker punches way above it’s weight. I use it mainly with my Samsung Galaxy phone and strictly LDAP. Everything else is disabled in the software/app that FiiO provides. And that is my second gripe. The ES100 rules on the app side. If FiiO put some time and money into providing similar functionality into their red headed stepchild app they could ask twice the price and I’d still think it was a bargain. But all the gripes aside it is definitely a step up from the ES100. Some told me if you have the Radsone that you’re good to go, no need to buy the FiiO. Fiddlesticks, BahHumbug and all those other quaking aphorisms. Buy it. It will make you smile.
text_fidelity_b: FiiO BTR5-384K/32Bit Native DSD256 Hi-Res CSR8675 Bluetooth5.0 Receiver/USB DAC/DSD Headphone Amp with LDAC, aptX HD, aptX, AAC (3.5mm Unbalanced&2.5mm Balanced Output, Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Roku 3 Streaming Media Player (2014 model) For the search feature alone you should buy this Roku. Instead of searching Netflix, Hulu, Amazon Prime for a title or actor you just search in one place and it finds everything. I searched for Benedict Cumberbatch and it found everything with him in it that was available for me. It even found something on HBO GO, which I never would have normally searched. I could click on a movie title and see what services it was one (and which ones I had free access to and which ones I would have to pay for it on). It's a truly revolutionary experience in finding digital content and I hope someone can duplicate it in online format.

In addition I find the remote super simple. The buttons make sense and they are in a good configuration. I love the headphone jack in the remote for watching things at night without bothering anyone else.

While there are a lot of channels, don't expect to find some new source of great content. You will still use the services you are using now (i.e. Netflix), you just have them in an easy, nice format.

I've previously purchased a Western Digital Media Hub for my father one year as a holiday present and within months it stopped letting him see Netflix on his TV (it's main purpose). I'm strongly considering buying him a Roku to replace it.
text_fidelity_b: Roku 3 Streaming Media Player (2014 model)

text_fidelity_a: Panasonic DMC-ZS40S Digital Camera with 3.0-Inch LCD (Silver) I only have the camera a short time, but so far I am very happy with it. Purchased it as a "throw in the purse" camera, as carrying my mirrorless camera with lenses or DSLR just isn't always warranted, but I often miss a camera when I don't bring one. I used a borrowed zs20 on a trip to Peru when my Samsung NX300 died, and loved the panoramic feature and great zoom. The superzoom on this camera is amazing. Just took it to try out on the beach and caught some great shots of birds without scaring them away (see the one legged bird in the attached). Color seems great. I could see taking this as the only camera on a trip. A recent photo enthusiast, so I can't address all of the technical issues, and haven't tried the macro feature etc., so cannot comment on all modes,  but for someone who wants a reasonably small camera with a lot of features, I recommend this one. Has all of the modes available, Aperature and Shutter priority, Auto, Program and Manual, as well as tons of "scene" modes. Range of settings more limited than my other cameras, but this isn't the same type of camera. I am returning the DMC ZS35 I first purchased (20X zoom), because this one has an EVF (hate fighting the washed out display on a sunny day when there is no EVF) and 30X zoom. It was worth the extra money. Purchased used from Amazon warehouse, so happy with the price.
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic DMC-ZS40S Digital Camera with 3.0-Inch LCD (Silver)

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Fire HDX 7", HDX Display, Wi-Fi and 4G LTE, 16 GB - Includes Special Offers (Previous Generation - 3rd) I update to the latest Kindle every year. The HDX 7" is great with Wi-Fi. I like the 64 GB and quad core processor. The dual band wi-fi can use more power than my Internet can really deliver. I will probably have to update my whole Internet package. When I use the wi-fi to do downloads, everything on my wi-fi slows to a crawl and my Internet movies on Amazon and home computer freeze till it is done. I think my phone company only offers 100 Mbps with my current package. This kindle is powerful and takes over my whole Wi-Fi service.
The power adapter is a little different this year and goes in at an angle (thought it didn't fit). The adapter comes with the Kindle.
I will be keeping my old Kindle Fire HD, because I still enjoy it and some of the old apps I am not tired of yet (not compatible to HDX). I will be able to upload more of my pdf's to this newer Kindle, because pdf's use a lot more space. Also I can download more TV shows and movies, since I live in the Amazon ecosystem.
I like the clock on the screen is back. When I open the Kindle cover, the clock is in the corner with the date. That was not on the HD, but was on the first Fire (it was bigger).
I like the offers, because it is important to me what else is available. The screen is beautiful as always. I did have to make some adjustments to brightness (using settings) and the books (using view) I am reading. Actually for us older folks, brighter is better.
The sound is nice. I was watching PBS channel out in my yard and my neighbors could hear it. The PBS channel app was not something I was aware of before, but loving it now (even with my Internet service).
The HDX is smaller than the HD 7", but the screen is still the same size.
The camera on the 7"HDX is better than the HD. I really like it, because it comes with its own app, and I don't have to download a free app like last year. The one on my 7" HD has problems but was free.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Fire HDX 7", HDX Display, Wi-Fi and 4G LTE, 16 GB - Includes Special Offers (Previous Generation - 3rd)

text_fidelity_a:
Leather Centric 15 Inch Buffalo Leather Laptop Messenger Bag Office Briefcase College Bag Fits Upto 14 Inch This is a retro leather laptop messenger bag - the material is made from something called "Buffalo" leather, which feels rough and stiff - quite the opposite of lambskin or buttery soft leather. The buckles are only for show because you can open and close the bag without unbuckling it, as there are buttons underneath. It has a weathered look, with varying shades of brown and sienna that give the impression that you're an Indiana Jones-type adventurer who's been carrying this bag through the outback, escaped tigers and bears, and came through fine, though the bag is a bit battered.

In other words, it's very manly, and harks back to the 1940s when bulky items were the norm because thinner materials hadn't been invented yet. While it looks great and seems well made (it's from India), it's actually limited in terms of actual everyday use. If you're traveling a lot, you want things to be as lightweight as possible. This is not one of those items. Even when empty, it feels cumbersome to carry. Stuffed with a laptop and papers, it will be heavy.

Think about it - when was the last time you actually saw someone on the train or airport carrying one of these? You might say you'd like to do so because it will make you look unique. In reality, other people may have tried carrying one of these and gave up.

So while it's nice as a conversation piece and something you might want to show off to your friends, I fear it will be one of those novelty items that, after its newness has worn off, will be relegated to the back of the closet.
text_fidelity_b: Leather Centric 15 Inch Buffalo Leather Laptop Messenger Bag Office Briefcase College Bag Fits Upto 14 Inch

Polaroid Cube HD 1080p Lifestyle Action Video Camera (Black) [Discontinued by Manufacturer] I was rather surprised when I got this with how small it is. I knew from the product description that it would be a little guy, but didn't have an appreciation for how small it was until I got it. It's a cube that is less than 1.5 inches on each side. Very compact, but it feels very solid and well-made.

Despite the compact size this is a solid performer. The video quality is quite clear and vivid provided you keep the cam steady. That's not easy to do if this is handheld given the small size, but it's designed to be mounted (there's a magnet in the base plus there are a variety of options available for mounting. Note that the mounts are sold separately).

The sound quality is good. Not spectacular, but reasonably clear and on a par with most cams I've used that have an internal mic.

Getting to the SD card is where the small size does cause a problem - it's not all that easy if you don't have nimble fingers (which I do not). You need to open the access door (which is sealed for water resistance) with a coin.

It doesn't have a lot of features which I find to be a plus since it greatly simplifies operation - the interface is a single button that turns it on/off, takes a still or starts/stops video recording. Can't get easier than that!

Minor quibbles aside, this is a solid performer and one that's well worth considering if you're looking for a very unobtrusive cam that's easy to operate (other than getting the SD card in and out). 4.5 stars rounded up to 5 due to the performance at this price point.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Polaroid Cube HD 1080p Lifestyle Action Video Camera (Black) [Discontinued by Manufacturer]

text_fidelity_a: SamData 32GB USB Flash Drives 4 Pack 32GB Thumb Drives Memory Stick Jump Drive with LED Light for Storage and Backup (4 Colors: Black Blue Green Purple) This unit does work, but it is too slow for me to recommend it to others. When writing music onto it from my Windows computer, the write speed was slow enough to repeatedly drop the data transfer rate all the way to zero. Other manufacturers' flash drives do not do that; they keep on going. The read speed is slow enough that it causes my car's infotainment system (2019 model year) to sometimes hang up. Indeed, at one point, it caused my backup camera to go to all black for a minute or two. Note that some other reviewers are apparently unware of what flash memory is like. It has a limited number of times that it can be written (rewritten), and it will wear out if you try to use it as a substitute for a SSD. It also isn't going to be nearly as fast as a SSD. Flash memory is most appropriate for putting mp3 files into your car's infotainment system and other applications that are write only a few times but read many times.
text_fidelity_b: SamData 32GB USB Flash Drives 4 Pack 32GB Thumb Drives Memory Stick Jump Drive with LED Light for Storage and Backup (4 Colors: Black Blue Green Purple)

It's a little more expensive than similar M/F 3.5 mm cables, but the build quality is also well above the typical cable. Well worth considering if you're looking for a cable that can stand up to a good measure of hard use.

text_fidelity_a:
Kikkerland UL03-A Universal Travel Adapter, Black I ended up returning these. I'm going to France and the UK, which have different plug styles. I thought this would be a pretty cool way to get an adapter for each country in one neat little gadget. Well, it looks like it would work fine, but it's twice as big as a standard simple one-piece adapter. So, for size and weight, it works out the same as having a simple adapter for France and a simple adapter for the UK. And it's more than twice the price of two simple adapters, so for price it's worse. Independent of price, it doesn't make sense to me to have something complicated when there aren't any advantages over the simple solution. I'm concerned that the complexity just adds more ways for something to go wrong, and the last thing you want to do on a trip is add more ways for something to go wrong.

So, I don't think this product makes any sense if you just need on or two plug styles. However, you would start seeing a benefit if you need three or more different plug styles on your trip.
text_fidelity_b: Kikkerland UL03-A Universal Travel Adapter, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Xiaomi YDXJ01FM Mi 4K Action Camera, 2.4” Touchscreen WiFi Sports Camera with Sony Image Sensor, 145° Wide Angle 4K/30fps 1080P/100fps Video Raw Image, Black I really wanted to like this camera. Construction quality is better than most budget-priced 4K action cameras. Price is much lower than GoPro. Battery life is great. Video quality is good for this price (but noticeably worse than GoPro and it lacks the 4K 60fps mode that GoPro has). Unfortunately, audio quality is poor.

A smartphone app is required to use much of the camera's functionality, including setting up the camera and all the wireless control features. I was able to download the app (a huge 75MB download to my Android phone). The app will not work until you create an account on Xiaomi's server in China. I am reluctant to send any of my personal information to an overseas corporation, but even when I tried to do it, I was unable to create the account, even after an hour of trying. The app does not work at all if I cannot login to the account.

A few more negatives about this camera. While the video quality is very good for this price level, audio recording quality is mediocre. This camera comes with no accessories in the box, just the camera, battery, brief instruction manual (more of the manual is in the app that I cannot use), and a charging cable (micro-USB, not USB-C like most modern devices). The camera uses a standard 1/4 inch tripod mount, but there is no GoPro-style action mount that would be much more sturdy and reliable if you are attaching the camera to a bicycle or helmet. There is no case to protect the camera from dirt or weather or use it underwater. Amazon does not sell any accessories either, so I don't know how to use this camera in an action situation. One battery is included in the box, but battery life is less than 2 hours and I always carry spares with my other action cameras. Again, Amazon does not sell spares.

Because of all these limitations, I can only give this camera 2 stars right now. Maybe if the app mysteriously starts working at some point and Amazon starts selling accessories to make the camera more usable, then I will consider reviewing the camera again.

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic DMC-TS6A LUMIX WiFi Enabled Tough Adventure Camera (Blue) I’m a big fan of the Panasonic Lumix line of point and shoot cameras. I’ve been using one for years and, while it has limited features by today’s standards, it has yet to let me down. This latest one in the Lumix line offers a huge range of capabilities, provides outstanding image quality, but continues to suffer from a less than ideal user interface.

The camera comes with just the basics: the camera, a single battery, lanyard and a charger (plus manuals and software). I was a little disappointed right off the bat when I saw the charger. Unlike the older Lumix chargers that had a wall plug built into the charger than flipped out, this has a separate power cord. While that does make it easier to plug into the wall, it also means I have to remember to carry the cord with me to charge it.

Initial setup is straightforward, with the usual time/date setting. Since this has a GPS there’s also the need to go through initializing that option as well. All of these steps can be skipped, but you’ll be reminded to do so every time you power on the camera. It also displays a warning on screen about the waterproof limitations of the camera (and provides ample documentation as to what it can/can’t do re: underwater use).

The view screen is wonderful. Sharp, clear, and easy to read in all lightning conditions. The menu system will be familiar if you’ve ever used a Lumix camera but, if not, it’s still pretty straightforward. I still think Canon has the lead when it comes to having an intuitive point and shoot menu system, but Panasonic does a decent job. I like that with most options there’s a scrolling line of text that comes up to explain what the option is/does. That’s very helpful for options you don’t often use and need help with, but it does not interfere or slow down operation should you know exactly what you want to select.

I won’t list all the camera specs in this review since those are easily available in the listing and the Panasonic web site. Suffice it to say this offers a huge range of options and capabilities that cover pretty much any shooting situation. The Intelligent mode shooting scenario options (of which there are many) are helpful when you just want to point the camera and have it do everything else for you, including compensation for specialized lighting/scene situations. I especially like the macro option, which produced some impressive close-up shots that were sharply focused and clear even though I didn’t use a table-top tripod for stability but relied on the image stabilization features of the camera.

The video recording image quality is excellent good for a point and shoot cam. The performance of the built in mic is decent as well. This won’t compete with a dedicated HD cam, but for casual video shooting it’s a small, simple and easy to use setup that gets the job done pretty well.

The WiFi setup was surprisingly easy. I was dreading that since it often can be a bear, but this was quick and easy, and the included instructions were easy to follow. I use the WiFi option a lot since the USB port to connect to a PC is inside the camera (located under the battery compartment door). It’s done that way to maintain a water-tight shell, but is also means it can be hard to get to easily.

What has not been improved, and actually has slipped a bit, is the overall user interface (e.g., the buttons on the back). They continue to be small, hard to read, and don’t provide solid feedback that they have been pressed. Given that the camera is designed to be used in “rugged” conditions, larger buttons would have been a big plus, especially for zoom and the main menu keypad since those are used so often. Using the menu buttons is hard enough with bare hands; it’s impossible if you have gloves on.

I would certainly recommend this camera if you’re looking for a rugged point and shoot for outdoor use, but also if you’re looking for a high feature camera that never leaves the house. The performance and feature set are both excellent. The user interface brings my rating to four stars but performance and option-wise, this camera offers a lot for the price point.
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic DMC-TS6A LUMIX WiFi Enabled Tough Adventure Camera (Blue)

TCL 32S3700 32-Inch 720p Roku Smart LED TV (2015 Model) UPDATE 2/10/16: It has been 44 days since I first contacted TCL about my defective TV. It has been 17 days since I was told a new TV would be sent to me and would arrive in 5-7 days. I have had numerous phone calls and emails on 12/28, 12/29, 1/21, 1/25, 1/27, 1/30, 2/4, 2/5, and 2/8. Each time TCL is unable to answer my questions (has new tv been shipped, what is tracking number) and each time I talk with someone I am repeatedly put on hold and then dismissed because they can't answer my questions and cant confirm what is going on. This has been extremely frustrating and the time period, lack of communication within the company, and conflicting instructions told to me by employees are all unacceptable. I loved the TV but it failed and trying to get resolution from this company has been a nightmare.

UPDATE 1/25/16 7PM: About an hour after updating my review I was contacted by TCL. After two phone conversations and several emails a replacement is being processed with no shipping costs at my expense. If this occurs in the timely fashion expected, I will update my review and ratings accordingly.

UPDATE 1/25/16: A week after I got the TV it started having display problems. The screen would come on so dark that only by looking at it at a certain angle could you tell that it was on. It required a jiggle/tap on the top for the image to flicker on all the way. I contacted amazon tech support. They had me try a power off/unplug. I expressed concern that it appeared to be something internal failing. They said the recorded my comments and were willing to offer a refund. I really wanted a replacement and not a refund so I said I'd see if it stopped acting up. It did not. It got progressively worse and now never turns on correctly and no longer results to tapping and jiggling the TV. On

12/28 I emailed TCLsocial regarding my problem as it was getting worse. On 12/29 they responded asking for a phone number so they could call me. I immediately responded with my phone number. I received no calls. I was then extremely busy workign 16-18hr days 7 days a week. The next chance I got, I emailed them again 1/21. They responded that they hadn't received my phone number. I sent it again. They said I would "get a call within the day". As of 1/25 no calls, no missed calls, no voicemails no emails. I'm fed up. All I wanted was for them to replace my manufacturing defective item with a new one. Its terrible how poor their response at getting this dealt with has been. At least I know Amazon will make the refund quick and easy. But I will most certainly not be using the money to get another TCL brand if this is how they treat their customers. Picture below is my screen on "on". If you squint you can see a faint outline of the netflix box to the right of the flash reflection. This is not a brightness or display setting issue.

ORIGINAL REVIEW: Excellent TV, very simple and fast set up. Beautiful picture and great sound. Love the smart tv features. I have never and likely will never have cable, this TV allows me to access my netflix and amazon as well as use chromecast to access my hbo go and youtube. I do not have a roku device or account but I love this TV's features. The remote is a nice small size and very simple and intuitive. I highly recommend this model and am very satisfied thus far. The stand/base is very solid and easy to put together. The remote came with new batteries. The customization and ease of use of this TV are wonderful. Price was great and shipping was fantastic.
text_fidelity_b: TCL 32S3700 32-Inch 720p Roku Smart LED TV (2015 Model)

text_fidelity_a: Logitech K750 Wireless Solar Keyboard for Mac — Solar Recharging, Mac-Friendly Keyboard, 2.4GHz Wireless - Silver I normally don't write many negative reviews especially for products that I didn't by from Amazon.  I bought this at a local store as I needed it asap for work. This is amazing in the initial period. I had no problems with wearing out or spring action- feels very good.  Function keys are ideal and the solar app/ light are great resources for letting you know when it is not getting enough light.  I used this on my 2015 MBP for the last two years, but towards the end of second year, it started to "randomly fail" for a few hours at a time.  I ultimately learned that I had to put it in heavy direct sunlight for about 30 minutes to "jump start" it.  I would put it on the car dash in the northern winter to do this (didn't get too cold or hot).  I then had it stop on a dark day and couldn't jump start it-- I tried everything including putting it under a shop light for a bit.  I finally broke down and contacted Logitech.  Now keep in mind that I registered it when I bought--  they suddenly are claiming it was outside of warranty even though I had registered it.  They are telling me to contact the store, but they have no way to pull it up as the store I bought it at is out of business and I paid cash.  I'm really frustrated as I went back and forth with them for almost two months.  I'm at the point where I am keeping the service ticket open as my way of giving them drama.  I ultimately bought the special rechargeable battery that it takes and replaced it despite warnings even on the battery not to do so.  It works for the most part.  I really wish Logitech would address the issue.  I'm also bummed that now that I am on an MBP 2017 15" that they are not making the unifying receiver in USB-C.  I would not recommend this as they have the same issue with the battery as Apple.  I want to rate it for the good times, but I just can't do it.  As you know once you get accustomed to a keyboard it is very hard to change.  Keep looking my friend, keep looking.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech K750 Wireless Solar Keyboard for Mac — Solar Recharging, Mac-Friendly Keyboard, 2.4GHz Wireless - Silver

MOS Magnetic Cable Organizer- Black I’ve got a few devices now, as probably every body reading this. A smartphone, a tablet, and a cordless mouse that plugs in to charge every week or two. And a couple U.S.B. cords hanging around is a mess. First to find one when needed. Then where to stash it after the use. This little gizmo is the best.
When I first saw it, I’m thinking. Why didn’t I do something like this. And even now, since I have already seen the idea. I could make something like this out of stuff I have around this room. But it’s not expensive. So I want to try and see if they did ‘good’ work. Well, they did.
I really wondered how, a magnetic mount like this could be safe around computers. I thought that the magnetic force might be so pathetically small, as to render such a device useless. But, the little triangle thing, that is the home base for your cable collection; is also magnetized. So a small magnet on the cord, along with the magnetic flux of the mounting surface, makes for a ‘good’ grip. For cables, such as designed for, is perfect. I wanted to put a set of headphones up on this rack. But it never happened. Sure, they would stick, and hold. But then, when other cables would be attached, and detached, the headphones would fall. But cords, are a rock solid stick.
And it is pretty. I’m no designer, but I think it makes my desk look like I care. And it’s a conversation piece. I really like this piece. But I still think, I should have thought of this.
text_fidelity_b: MOS Magnetic Cable Organizer- Black

Moshi AirFoil Screen Protector for Kindle Paperwhite, Kindle, and Kindle Keyboard (2 Pack) Even though I’ve had my various Kindles for years and never gotten a scratch on any of them, I thought it would be nice to have a screen protector so that I could feel more confident throwing my beloved Paperwhite in my purse and taking it on the go. I have also been reading with slightly dirtier hands since I have a new baby, so once again, the screen protector seemed like a good idea to keep it from getting mucked up with drool or whatnot.

The thing that sold me on this particular screen protector is that it makes the claim that it has a permeable surface, so air bubbles don’t get stuck under it during installation. I didn’t find that to be true. Maybe I did something wrong, but I needed to carefully apply it and I used a credit card to apply even pressure to get the bubbles out. Bubbles did not magically disappear nor were they any easier to get out, despite the claim to the contrary.

That said, this is no harder to install than a screen protector on your phone. It’s a bit of a pain, you have to make sure your cats aren’t anywhere nearby, and you have to have meticulously clean hands and very good lighting to make sure you don’t get dust or junk stuck underneath. But once it’s installed, it does exactly what it’s supposed to, and the screen is still very responsive. I really don’t notice it, beyond knowing that my screen is now protected.

Overall, though it doesn’t live up to the hype of being easier to install than other screen protectors, this is a perfectly serviceable product that does what it is supposed to.
text_fidelity_b: Moshi AirFoil Screen Protector for Kindle Paperwhite, Kindle, and Kindle Keyboard (2 Pack)

text_fidelity_a:
REOLINK 4K Security Camera Outdoor System, Surveillance IP PoE Camera with Human/Vehicle/Pet Detection, 25FPS Daytime, 100F IR Night Vision, Work with Smart Home, Up to 256GB SD Card, RLC-810A Fantastic camera. One of those items that screamed quality right out of the box. Good build, compact size, and has a waterproof connector for your Ethernet cable. Can be mounted where the cable comes through a hole in a fascia board behind the camera or where the cable comes out the side of the base. Base is infinitely adjustable. Camera has slight overhang on the top to keep water off the lens. Three pigtail cables - RJ-45 female connector can be the single cable if you have PoE or you can power this via a 12v power adapter or cable (local or centralized) for versatility.

This is my first IP camera, but I've used many analog cameras and DVRs.

I've hooked this up three ways: By itself, to a switch on the same network as a stand-alone NVR, and to a switch on the same network utilizing my QNAP NAS as the NVR - in each case powered by PoE. Here are some details I've figured out in the process:

---By itself: You can view it quickly and easily without delay with the App, which seems to have all the things you'd expect from a camera viewing app. I assume you can record to or snapshot to an SD card from the description, but I'm going to record to my network, so I didn't try that feature. This was just plug and play, worked super easy.

What I love is that once you figure out the IP address, you can access the camera via a webserver, which pretty much future-proofs the hardware. I despise "smart" devices where you need an app, because then you're at their mercy to run their app on whatever OS they decide to use and they can force you to make accounts, update, etc. Having this open to the user/owner is the way to go. Bravo.

And that web server is full featured. I was able to play around and do everything here before I bothered downloading the app.

Note that - like every camera I've ever used - the viewing software sends a substream which is lower resolution unless you demand the higher resolution. With the app you can see low and medium resolution, but 4k has trouble playing over WiFi (or else it's just smart enough to realize my screen can't support it anyway). Just pointing this out so you realize if you're seeing pixels, that doesn't mean the camera isn't actually recording at 4k.

---With NVR: I recently acquired a cheap 8-channel 4k NVR that I believe to be a Uniview OEM. I added a hard drive and put it on the same network as this camera. The NVR has an 8 port PoE switch built in, but it must also be a router, because it wants to use a different subnet if you put the camera on the NVR's switch. Otherwise, you can easily point the NVR to the camera via IP address.

So...if you point the NVR to the camera via IP address, you can view the camera from its own app or from the NVR app. I assume this still takes one of the NVRs 8 channels. This might be useful if you want to give someone access to just one camera on your network. But it occurred to me that, setup this way, you have constant data streaming over your network, and after you add quite a few cameras in 4k, this is going to start adding up.

If you put the camera directly on the NVR, you'll have to change the IP manually to match the subnet, or maybe you'll somehow get it to work through the NVR or with DHCP. I hadn't bothered spending time figuring this out yet because at the time I thought I'd just use my other switch, but I'm thinking once I get more cameras, it'll probably make more sense to put them directly onto the NVR and ...actually, then I won't have to change my entire IP scheme since I won't have so many new devices to organize.

I'm certain I can get it all working in unison with no problem, but it is more complicated than if you just buy an NVR set with a bunch of cameras already ready to work together. Either way shouldn't be a problem if you have IP knowledge, but I'm guessing a random homeowner might prefer a set.

---Using my NAS as NVR. Hmmm...a little disappointed with QNAP in this regard. I mean, I have three NASs, and I'm assuming they all have 2 licenses included, but to combine them into one program then I believe requires yet another license. I'm not into licenses, even if they're a one time deal, because that means you need accounts and if something happens where they're lost, you can run into all kinds of other issues. I just think consumers need to stand up to this sort of thing. But anyway, I had two included, so I tried it out:

I realized that this is a lot of work for my little consumer grade NAS, and even if I had a more hardcore NAS, I'm not sure I want resources being used all the time. It seems like I couldn't get it to use H.265 compression, nor could I get it to record at the higher resolutions and frame rates. Again, I didn't play with this too awful much once I got it recording and working because I already realized I definitely like the stand alone DVR better. The QNAP even had extra stuff to download and windows to pop up on your PC and all this other stuff. Just not as streamlined as I had hoped.

----Conclusion is that the camera is awesome. I'm not sure many are any better at this point. If you want something that just works easy and you don't know much about networking, you may wish to just buy an NVR set. But if you are IP capable, I think buying components separately could be a great way to go because you can really customize what you want to do. But as always, more options with networking means more potential headaches. But I am pretty certain that once you get it working the way you want it, you should be able to forget all about it and have it work indefinitely.

Oh, and after all that, I shouldn't forget to point out that I'd be thrilled to have this all by itself watching my porch just so I can tell when there's a package out there. My Ring (that came with the house) can't even see that because of the angle it is set at.
text_fidelity_b: REOLINK 4K Security Camera Outdoor System, Surveillance IP PoE Camera with Human/Vehicle/Pet Detection, 25FPS Daytime, 100F IR Night Vision, Work with Smart Home, Up to 256GB SD Card, RLC-810A

HP Sprocket Portable Color Photo Printer, Print Social Media Photos on 2x3" Sticky-Backed Paper - Black (X7N08A) This is a great improvement over an earlier-gen ZINK paper ("zero ink") portable printer we have, which requires a wired connection and a proprietary charger, and no longer holds a charge well.

The HP Sprocket connects and prints wirelessly, charges from a standard micro-USB cable, and has a lithium-ion battery which is sure to last a lot longer.

We had it unboxed and printing in less than 5 minutes. You run it from a free app available for Android or Apple iOS devices. We used the Android version and it works great.

It takes less than 30 seconds to wirelessly send and print a photo. The prints are 2 inches by 3 inches, smooth and glossy, good resolution, and have a peel-and-stick backing for quick and easy mounting. In the long run, the priciest thing about a ZINK printer is the paper, so shop around for deals.

The prints came out a little to the warm side in color when sent "as is," but the app allows a lot of enhancement and has lots of effects you can add.

text_fidelity_a:
NEW Microsoft Surface Headphones 2 - Light Gray I'm not an audiophile, but I've tried out a good number of different earbud brands lately, all across the quality spectrum. I'm grading on a curve here.

Packaging is sufficient. A few tip sizes, quick start, instructions, and whatever is in that other manual of junk I always throw away. The earbud case is lozenge shaped and pocketable enough. No external lights, which is nice if you're charging it next to your bed, but not so much if you want to know their charge status.

They are supposed to immediately start trying to bluetooth pair with something when first opened, and appeared to be trying to do so. My Surface was unable to locate them. I even tried with a second Surface. I plugged in the case and left it to charge for 15 minutes, and then they paired fine. Overall on unboxing and setup, I'd say they're adequate, but far from exceptional.

The earbuds themselves are aggressively visible. I assume they're trying to ride the I-Pod branding success, but I'm not really feeling it. Despite looking huge, they don't feel huge. They are lightweight and comfortable. They don't feel like they are going to fall out, despite not feeling like they're crammed in the ear. Fit is unusual in that you can turn the earbud like a screw to make it tighter or looser. Sound is good. I'm giving them very low marks for appearance, and very good for fit and sound.

These use swipe style controls, which I despise. I much prefer a physical button that I can just feel that I've clicked. The controls do work as advertised, but there's enough delay that it often takes me a while of swiping my ear and waiting until it gets the message. Mostly irritating when someone tries to talk to me and I can't get it to pause for several seconds.

Range is average.

Overall, Id' say there's a bit of a brand name premium on the price compared to some other products, and I'm saying that as someone who has used Surface products as my primary computers for many years now, but they're not bad. I've definitely tried more expensive earbuds that weren't as good, but of what I've tried, I'm happiest so far with the Jabra Elite series of earbuds.
text_fidelity_b: NEW Microsoft Surface Headphones 2 - Light Gray

Samsung Gear Fit2 Smartwatch Large, Black After struggling with an early incarnation of a Fitbit, this watch is a breeze. I honestly do not understand the negative reviews, unless a few lemons were sent out.

It couldn't be easier, because the app explains everything and walks you through the process. It's well thought-out and intuitive.
And while the primary goal is as a fitness watch, which it excels at, I really get a kick out of the fact that I can get all my push notifications on it, and even read emails and texts on it.
But back to Fitness. Of course, it acts as a pedometer. But it also measures your heartbeat, every 5 minutes. This thing keeps track of everything! It even knows what kind of exercise you're doing. It maps out progress so that it's easier to keep an eye on where your goals are and how to meet them.
It's synced to my Samsung Galaxy phone, and it plays all of the music that I've got on my phone.

While it is not waterproof, it is water resistant. I'm one of those people that washes my hands a lot, and I haven't had any problem with water sprinkling on it.
Right now I split my time between two locations. The GPS works great in the Midwest, yet is pretty dicey in Wyoming. Since that isn't a big issue for me, no star is subtracted. This is a quality product that does all I want it to do, and more.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Gear Fit2 Smartwatch Large, Black

They both charge easy and keep a great charge. The case feels cheaper with these newer 3's and the earbud itself feels cheaper. Cheaper, but at the same time lighter which is a good thing. The color offerings are also not as good as the Active 75t's were. THESE earbuds are dark grey, one of 4 colors offered and just look like standard earbuds in color.

I think the main difference between the two is the active 75ts are more designed to be waterproof, sweatproof, and for sports. THESE Elite 3's are more basic.

I like these Jabra lines because once they are on and music is playing you cannot hear the world around you. Husband's private calls ... GONE. I can be in our small house and he can conduct his business privately. Definitely a plus. Music sounds great, everything sounds great. Have not use them for calls.

Overall ... these are worth the price. Best part is how they fit and stay in my ears. I would not hesitate to recommend these to someone and I, for one, have no regrets.

Azio PRISM USB Wired Keyboard with 7 Colorful Backlights, Black (KB507) Overall, this is a decent full-size USB keyboard. The keys are nicely sized and have a medium length throw. There’s little tactile feedback, making the keys feel rather mushy. But, on the plus side, it’s 100% silent in use – no clicky sound of any type.

The layout is a standard QWERTY with a separate number key pad and F1 to F12 at the top. There’s also a separate pad for cursor up/down/right/left.

The back light is very nice and has the unique feature in that you can change the color. There are several to pick from including a “mixed” mode that has several colors making for a rainbow look. Color selection is easy via a dedicated key at the top of the keyboard. Just press it to cycle through the colors. The back light can also be set to off.

The build quality is decent. It’s all plastic and pretty lightweight, but durable enough for normal use. There’s a kick stand on the back that folds out to prop up the keyboard at a comfortable angle, and non-skid feet to hold it in place. I had no problems with this staying put even when banging away at full typing speed. There is some flex in the frame when typing with force, but nothing horrible.

There’s a small area for resting your palm, but it’s rather short to provide much (if any) ergonomic support.

It does not have any indicator lights such as for caps lock, num lock, etc.

Installation is simple on a Win machine -- just a plug-and-play with no drivers needed.

While the overall design is nice and I love the back light feature (plus the ability to change colors), the lack of tactile feel and the lack of status indicator lights drops my rating to 4 stars. Still well worth considering as a replacement full-size USB keyboard, especially if you’re looking for a 100% silent keyboard.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Azio PRISM USB Wired Keyboard with 7 Colorful Backlights, Black (KB507)

PANASONIC Wings Sport Headphones are Ultra-Light Wireless Bluetooth Sport Earbud 3D Flex Sport Clips with Microphone and Call/Volume Controller, IPX5 Rated Water-Resistant - RP-BTS35-K (Black) I received these earphones from Amazon Vine in early January, 2018. I liked the over-the-ears design. It makes the earphones far less likely to fall off when exercising. The sound quality is also excellent. I found its wireless bluetooth function quite handy for listening to music on my smartphone while walking, biking, lifting weights or doing calisthenics.

In short, as long as the battery could be charged, these sport earphones worked quite well. But suddenly, a few weeks ago, after only 7 months of use, the battery simply would no longer take a charge. The manual says that the battery should last through up to 300 charges, and there is absolutely no way that in only seven months I charged this device 300 times. It holds a charge well while the battery is working, much better than the other bluetooth earbuds that I have owned. So I could use it for up to five days without charging the battery. This means that, in seven months, I only charged the battery about 42-50 times, at most. This means the life of the battery was a mere 16% of what the manufacturer promised!

This is not a device in which the battery can be replaced. Therefore, once the battery dies, the earphones are worthless. Since the warranty is only for 90 days, there is no recourse with the manufacturer for replacing this device after that length of time.

The way that this product works is a good idea, but until the design includes the possibility of replacing the battery, the high price is simply not worth it. I will have to stick to cheap earbuds which are not such a hit to my pocketbook when their non-replaceable battery dies.

I rate this product as follows:

Sound quality 5 stars
Durability of battery: 1 star
Value for price: 1 star
Overall average: 2.3 stars

text_fidelity_a:
Corsair Vengeance 2000 Wireless 7.1 Gaming Headset (CA-9011115-NA) The first thing to know is this is for PC gaming (and other PC use). It will not work on the XBox 360 and it will only work as a voice headset (not carrying game sounds) on the PS3.

The picture doesn't do the comfort of these justice. That microfiber lining on the ear buds feels like velvet. It is so nice on the head. They're light. They're comfortable. They adjust to your head size and are angled just a bit for maximum comfort.

The microphone does not fully swivel. You can only wear it on the one side, but that helps, because the headset will do an excellent job of emulating surround sound and you don't want to hear your enemy coming at you from the left, when in fact they are on the right and your headset is reversed. Don't ask me how many times I've done that. Games are substantially better with surround sound. I was used to "there is a noise somewhere so look around". This takes it to "there is a noise just left of me so look left" which is both helpful and more immersive. These headphones do a great job with that. It is emmulation but the games I've tried it on (mostly with Steam) are able to handle the fact that the PC is performing emulation and accomodate. I'm spending less time wondering what's killing me and more time returning fire.

When I'm not gaming with them, I use them for Skype, most particularly for seemingly endless conference calls. The battery can outlast my coworkers' ability to drag out a call, and with my coworkers, that's impressive. I can walk from room to room, answer the door, get another cup of coffee (and then lunch, and then dinner) and never miss a thing. Moving the microphone up will mute it (great for dealing with whomever is at the door) and the wheel on the side can adjust the volume (perfect for when the discussion devolves into a shouting match). The microphone has excellent pickup.

They're also great for watching videos without distrubing anyone else, and the surround sound emulation works perfectly there as well. There is some sound leak, but not much. For music, they provide excellent range and purity of sound.

Some days I spend more time with these things on my head than off. They're comfortable enough, and last long enough, for me to do that.
text_fidelity_b: Corsair Vengeance 2000 Wireless 7.1 Gaming Headset (CA-9011115-NA)

Logitech H390 Wired Headset for PC/Laptop, Stereo Headphones with Noise Cancelling Microphone, USB, In-Line Controls, Works with Chromebook - Black I got this headset to practice working with speech recognition software such as Dragon NaturallySpeaking. Overall, I've been surprised and incredibly impressed with the performance. The recognition is better than with the standard headset that came with the software, and the headset does everything I had hoped.

There's a volume control button on the cord, and the USB cord is about 8 feet long, which is plenty generous for connecting to my computer and doing speech recognition.

The only problem with this headset is that I want to use it for hours on end while narrating articles. I'm a freelance writer, and sometimes I either just don't feel like typing, have a sore wrist or fingers, or feel like I can narrate my thoughts faster than I can type them. After about two hours of using this headset, my ears start to ache. I haven't figured out any way of changing the tension on this headset so it doesn't press so hard on my ears.

While I would definitely recommend this headset as a low-budget alternative to higher end products, and for people who would like to use a headset for just an hour or so at a time, I would not recommend it for people who want to use the headset for any kind of professional or serious hobby endeavor. I had to use a separate diplexer to join my UHF and VHF antennas since this didn't provide both inputs. Unlike my other amp, though, this has an LTE filter built in - a product of its newness. Signal gauge is just a bit gimmicky, at least in my case where I'm pointing between two cities and trying to get as much as I can from each, which doesn't equal maximum signal according to this gauge. But that's okay. Use "TV Fool" and a compass, and you won't need a gauge, but it won't hurt.

text_fidelity_a:
Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa Hands-Free, 10.1" 1080p Full HD Display, 32 GB, Marine Blue (Previous Generation - 7th) I'm not going to delve into the technical aspects of the Fire as others have done an admirable job already. But as an alternative to other, more expensive tablets, the Fire is an amazing piece of tech.

I was almost getting ready to pull the trigger on the Google Pixel C or Samsung S3. A big leap for me as I didn't want to spend $500 plus on a tablet, but I wanted fast speed, large screen, and inexpensive aftermarket accessories.

The Fire is dual-core, so it flies through the games I play. A big plus. I know everyone hates when their game bogs down in the middle of a rousing Orc battle, or, even worse, won't even load. The Fire has run all the games I've thrown at it with no issues.

The 10" screen is heavenly, considering I came from a generic 7" tablet that was VGA on a good day. The text is crisp, the graphics flow as they should. HD movies and shows are freakin' excellent. The 10" format seems to be the best for this.

If you research well for accessories, you can find some nice deals. There was no way I was going to spring for a $30 case, when the $10 Fintie case works as good or better. More money saved for movies, games, and books!

Please don't spend the extra $15 on the 'without special offers' option. The only special offers thrown at you are when the tablet wakes from sleep. A quick swipe and they're gone. Save that money for a case!

And yes, Virginia, you can get the google play store. The easiest way is to install 4 app files and run them in order. No rooting, no PC hookups. Go to blog.ebook-reader dot com and search 'how to install google play on fire.' Easy peasy, just follow the instructions to the letter.

All-in-all this a capable tablet offered by Amazon. The price is right, the tech is excellent considering its price point. You can game like a madman, watch shows, and read War & Peace.
text_fidelity_b: Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa Hands-Free, 10.1" 1080p Full HD Display, 32 GB, Marine Blue (Previous Generation - 7th)

text_fidelity_a:
Ring Video Doorbell Pro – Upgraded, with added security features and a sleek design (existing doorbell wiring required) Great Addition to Home Security System

First I should say there is no 100% perfect home security system. That is why I have a home security “solution” that incorporates several different, but tied together systems. I have a full Lorex Camera System, Smart Things Hub and a wired alarm system. But even with all that there was something missing. If I wasn’t home, all of the other items were only good after the fact. Meaning I could see who was at my door, or in my house after I got back home. Sure I could set alerts on those other devices, but when your phone chirps 10 alerts per hour, it just becomes white noise. These other systems had so many false positives I ultimately turned them off.

Pros: But the Ring Bell filled several voids in these other systems. One, the false positives are almost nonexistent due to the ability to mask the alert area of the camera. My existing security system may alert me, but then I had to log into the camera system to see what was going on. The time it takes to do that could make a real difference. The ability to answer and interact with someone who rings your bell from your couch or from at work is invaluable! The person ringing the bell has no idea where you are answering from. But the best part is being able to ignore solicitors and screen people before you answer. It’s as easy as answering a phone call and the live image is instantaneous. The fact that it integrates with my SmartThings hub is just icing on the cake.

I was able to install the Ring Bell Pro in about 15 minutes following the simple instructions. It is extremely well thought out. The video quality of the Ring Pro is excellent! It does not have a very wide angle and there is a slight fisheye distortion, but it should be more than sufficient for most applications. The mobile app is also very intuitive. As I mentioned, when you get an alert, you can immediately see who is at the door and you can choose to answer and speak, or just watch.

Cons: I was confused by the wall plate not having the mounting holes line up with the existing wall plate holes. This required drilling holes above and below the existing holes to mount the plate. I could see no reason for this.

The unit can easily be ripped off the wall with one hand. Because the main unit mounts onto a plastic wall cover, it would take about 2 seconds to remove and disable the unit. But at least you will get an alert and when you went to log in you would know something was wrong. However, the Ring Pro has a unique purchase protection that sates “If your Ring™ Video Doorbell is stolen at any time after your purchase, Bot Home Automation, Inc. will replace your Ring™ Video Doorbell at no charge to you”. That’s pretty impressive!

If you want to keep your Ring History, you have to sign up for their paid service. Otherwise you only see live views. Prices vary by plan, but they do offer one free month for new customers.

Overall: There is no perfect security system. Each one has its plusses and minuses. But the Ring Pro should be part of every home security solution. Also, if I had to choose only one component for a complete home security solution, this would be high up on my list.

Update: 7/10/2017 - The unit has powered down several times and gone off line. This has required disconnecting it at the unit or the bell inside and reconnecting it. I have verified my power supply works OK. We will see if this becomes a ongoing issue.

Update: 10/30/2017 - I have downgraded from 5 to 3 starts today. First, the unit still stops working at times and needs to be rebooted by disconnecting the wires at the bell. The existing analog bell only chimes for the Ding and not the Dong. However the biggest disappointment is a inherent design flaw in the phone application. If someone come to the door and quickly goes away, like the UPS guy, by the time you take out your phone, open the app and connect, they are long gone. So you do get alerted, but there is no way to access the app fast enough to get a live view of what happened. You have to wait a few minutes until you can review the past activity, which requires a subscription. I guess it's still better than nothing.
text_fidelity_b: Ring Video Doorbell Pro – Upgraded, with added security features and a sleek design (existing doorbell wiring required)

text_fidelity_a:
D-Link DCS-934L Day & Night Wi-Fi Camera (Black) IP cameras have always been a total pain for me to get up and running. There’s always something that goes wrong, and I end up spending hours getting it to work. This model, however, was a dream to install. The installation quick-start guide is very clear, and offers two options: installing it if you have a D-Link router; or installation with a non-Dlink router. I used the non-Dlink router approach. You download an install program from the Dlink site that walks you through the installation in a clear, easy step-by-step fashion. I had it running in a couple of minutes in hard wired mode, and a couple minutes more to get it to run wirelessly. Very impressed with how easy it was.

The build quality of the camera itself is pretty good. It’s very lightweight but still feels sturdy, and comes with a stand that has a ball and socket joint so you can rotate and position the camera pretty much any way you would need it. The only hardware issue that I didn’t care for was the power cord. It’s rather short (about 4 foot), which limits where I can position the camera. A longer cord – at least 6 foot – would have been a lot nicer.

Using the camera is both easy and frustrating. There is a mobile app, but it’s really only to view the live feed and take snapshots on demand as you watch the live feed. For finer controls and adjustments you need to use a PC and the My D-Link site. That’s where things can be frustrating.

For example, on the settings page there is a clear section dedicated to email notifications with a checkbox. It is strongly implied that checking the checkbox will allow you to receive email notifications after you have set parameters for either motion detection or sound detection. However, after I set parameters for motion detection and then checked the box for email notifications, I did not receive any emails. After doing some searching via Google I found out that I needed to access the "advanced settings" and set up email there too. This was a far more complicated process and required more online research, but after a little bit of trial and error, I got the email notification working. You’ll need info such as the SMTP server address for your email client, the SMTP server port number, and two email addresses for yourself (one for the sender email; the other for the receiver email).

Why a product with such an easy install process has such a complicated usage setup (with much of the info needed not present on the D-Link site) is frustrating.

Once I got the email notification working, I could choose to have it send me an image at the moment of detection, or a set of 6 images (3 images just before detection and 3 images just after detection, at ½ or full second intervals). I can have it always on, or set it to detect only at certain periods of each day. So far I tried the 6 images option and have it always on, and that's worked out reasonably well.

Night vision and day vision seem to work well, with an acceptably clear picture. I have noticed that some times the view remains in night vision mode even when the room is sunny. Not sure why that is happening. Regardless, the picture remains clear.

It cannot record video captured since the camera does not have an SD card option.

You may need to play with the motion sensitivity adjustment and area of sensitivity to get something that works to your preference. I've found that sensitivity definitely needs to be adjusted higher for reliable night views, which means fiddling with the settings each day. While d-link allows you to adjust motion sensors on a day/night basis, it doesn't let you automatically set sensitivity for different times of the day, so that still has to be a manual task.

Although getting some features working is frustrating due to the lack of info on the D-link site, the overall ease of hardware installation, decent build quality, and good picture quality earn this 4 stars. If the D-Link site was improved this would be a five-star camera at this price point.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: D-Link DCS-934L Day & Night Wi-Fi Camera (Black)

PWR+ Laptop Table Stand Adjustable Riser: Portable with Mouse Pad Fully Ergonomic Mount Ultrabook MacBook Gaming Notebook Light Weight Aluminum Black Bed Tray Desk Book Fans Up to 17 inch This is a really nice laptop desk. The first thing that caught my eye was the construction quality. The table is metal and solid - no flexing at all, and built to take a pretty good pounding. The top has a "dimpled" finish that is stamped into the metal, so it's not something that will wear or fall off, like those stick-on pads.

It comes with a small side panel that can be hooked onto either side to use a mouse, trackball or other such device. It is also metal and very sturdy. It also has an adjustment knob so the extension can be tilted.

The desktop is about 16.5 inches wide and 11 inches deep (not including the extension, which is about 6.5 by 6 inches). It's a nice size for even a large laptop.

But what really sets this apart is the legs and how easy they are to configure. There are push-in buttons at the leg joints that allow the legs to be folded as needed. They click into place securely - no matter how much I jostled the table, the legs stayed firmly positioned where I put them.

On the downside, the legs are plastic. They are sturdy, but metal legs would have been wonderful.

The top has a raised lip on one side which is nice for holding the laptop if the table top is inclined. It also has a built-in dual fan to keep the heat down from the laptop. It runs off a USB port (cable is included). Unfortunately, it does not use a standard micro or mini USB input port on the fan but rather a pin-style port. This means you'll have to be sure to take the included cable along since you won't be able to make do with a standard USB cable.

The fans run very quietly. I didn't find the noise at all bothersome or even really noticeable. My laptop fan is actually louder than the desk fans.

Very pleased with this desk - very handy addition that has ample adjustability to keep my laptop positioned for easy use, and solid build quality to last for some time. Highly recommend.

text_fidelity_a:
Motorola CommandOne Bluetooth Headset - Retail Packaging One of the most important attributes for a headset is comfort. I've tried a few over the years, but always have found them to be a pain (literally!) if they are worn for more than 20 minutes or so. I'm very happy to report that the Moto is a dream when it comes to comfort - had it on for a three+ hour drive, and didn't even know it was there. Plus, it didn't cause a problem with my glasses, unlike other models I've tried.

Set up was very straightforward - basically just follow the prompts and it works. I didn't try out the text-to-voice feature but it sounds interesting. Not really something I would use since I don't text much at all, but if you're text-heavy, that feature would certainly be of value.

Audio quality was excellent. Had no problems hearing callers even with music playing in the car. Range was also very good.

My complaints are two-fold. First a minor one - this comes packed in what I would consider to be wasteful packaging. Looks impressive in a clear, thick plastic box, but the amount of materials used for packing is unnecessary. I did not, however, deduct anything from its rating due to that.

What did cause a loss of one star was the mic pickup. In a quiet environment it was fine. But, in a noisy environment (such as outside, in a crowded restaurant or with moderate-level music playing in the car), it picks up so much background noise that people had problems hearing me. To ensure this was actually the case, I loaned it to a friend and had him call me so I could hear for myself. It seems that the mic is either way too sensitive or not sufficiently directional - it truly is hard to hear the person's voice when they are using the headset should they be in anything other than a pretty quiet environment..

But, that aside, this is the best headset I've used to date. Especially recommended if you have had comfort issues with other headsets or are a glasses wearer.
text_fidelity_b: Motorola CommandOne Bluetooth Headset - Retail Packaging

Good Range

Usage is about as easy as can be: one dial for frequency; one dial for volume (and on/off). There's a tone switch that basically enhances the bass (it sounds much better with bass enhancement). It can switch between AM, FM and shortwave. FM reception is excellent. I could not, however, get anything other than static on the SW band (probably due to where I am located rather than the radio itself). It can run on batteries (not included) or an AC adapter (which is included).

The build quality is just OK. It doesn't have much of a solid feel to it, and is lightweight. This is not a radio you can toss around and expect it to make it through in good shape.

A great item to have on hand when the power goes out (provided you remember to stock up on batteries) or just to be able to listen to the radio without the Internet. Five stars.

Arlo Pro - Wireless Home Security Camera System with Siren | Rechargeable, Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, 2-Way Audio, Wall Mount | Cloud Storage Included | 1 camera kit (VMS4130) After initial euphoria, I have to say that the ROI is marginal at best. Briefly, here is why:

Positive:
1. Excellent day and night picture quality
2. Simple configuration and UI.
3. Free storage up to limit.
4. Rugged construction
5. Integration with Smarthings and other IoT.
6. Easy setup. Ensure you buy the condoms and mounting brackets for outside.

Negative: (Relative to price point)
1. Battery life is marginal. If you never have motion in an area great. But, think about that front yard where you have people walking by or cars parked just on the edge of your property. With roughly 10-15 activation per day, the battery drains quickly. I feel I would be better off with a perm. powered device.
2. While it has a standard micro usb port similar to virtually any android smart phone. You still require the Arlo plug to charge. Not a deal breaker, but painful.
2. App load times/camera viewing is slow. I have a 100 mb Xfinity internet connection with Netgear Orbi Mesh setup within 15 ft of the front camera. Connection in my house is not the issue. I have a Samsung S7 device. Be prepared to wait upwards of 30 seconds before authentication, app loads AND THEN the camera activates to see who is at the front door. It needs to be faster.
3. The absolute worst aspect of the camera is that recording does not start fast enough. Roughly 30 seconds of an event (or more) go by before capture begins. This is not acceptable. I have tried playing with various settings but unable to resolve.

Overall, I regret purchasing now. I should have invested the time and installed a fixed camera setup.

12-Jul-17 - I have lowered the stars on this product because of the incredibly poor support provided for both this product and in particular the ORBI which I also have. The warranty on both products which are similarly priced make zero sense. Stay away from NETGEAR until they get their act together.

17-Aug-17 - Finally heard back from NETGEAR and received confirmation in their user forums that the original screw adapter on the VMA1000 mount for the solar panel is too big. (gee thanks..I knew that) I was sent new screws that now allow the solar cable to be plugged in along with the VMA1000 mount. Why these are not highlighted everywhere and why there is no update to the Amazon listing as a bulletin or something to look for when buying the solar panel, I don't know. Overall, I would say NETGEAR is completely lost on any form of cohesive support and sincerely hope my product continues to work as I do not want to ever have to call or email again..

June 2020
I am done with Arlo. The product is over-priced and unreliable. Here is why:
I added the doorbells 2 yes ago and 2 of 2 have been rma'd.
2 of the cameras have been rma'd.
1 of the 2 solar panels has apparently died as not properly charging. This after less than 2 years.
I only realized recently that some Einstein at Arlo decided to have the wifi channel operate on the exact channel my mesh is on. There are clearly issues.
The camera has good and bad days from an access perspective. Some days they come up in about 30 seconds. Some they don't load..
The delay of 5 seconds before motion activates recording is brutal. You can completely someone moving fast.
Arlo support has become poor after being fantastic initially.

This product will be going the way of my Orbi soon. I am done with Netgear ( or formerly Netgear) products...

Philips BT2500B/37 Wireless Portable Speaker I have owned those annoying bluetooth ear pieces that always feel like they're about to fall off - or actually do. And although the sound varies from product to product, it's just not a system I am comfortable with.

This little speaker is simply perfect for my needs. It is 4 inches by 4 inches wide and only 1 inch thick. It has a switch that you slide to the right when you wish to enable the bluetooth, or to the left to turn it off. There is also another small button right beside the switch that you push in to receive or disconnect a call. A silver volume knob is sleekly incorporated in the overal design. The pairing was instant and consistant. No need to type in some code or wait forever for them to find each other. But here's the most important part - I hear my calls clearly and with no drop off or fade.

In all fairness, I only use this in my car and I don't spend ridiculous amounts of time on my phone when I'm driving. I've used other products with useless results. Half of the time I would risk a ticket by just ditching the ear piece and talking on my cell. In this case, I'm able to place it on the seat next to me and converse without any problems. Now that it's passed my tests, I'll be getting some velcro and mounting it to my dash board when I'm driving, and then just popping it in the glove compartment when I'm done.

The unit comes with a USB charger cable and it had a partial charge when I received it. Once it's fully charged and you turn it on, a blue light will blink for about 2 seconds and then go to a solid blue. According to the enclosed instructions, you will know that the battery is low when it blinks red. Couldn't be easier.

Musically speaking, my JBL and Sony are better designed for that purpose. But as a compact, speaker phone - this Phillips is without equal. Hands-free clarity without an annoying piece of plastic hanging over your ear. What more could you ask?
text_fidelity_b: Philips BT2500B/37 Wireless Portable Speaker

We fiddled and fiddled and did what it said, after reconnecting the internet we had to clear the data. This fixed it , and it is now working perfectly again. My only complaint is that troubleshooting information was hard to find. Even the error messages were not easy to understand. In spite of that, if it had needed to be replaced, I would have been counting the days. I love this thing. It's sooooooooooooo wonderful to be able to watch movies and TV series without commercials. The picture is crystal clear and it's really easy to use. The voice search works extremely well. There are tons of free shows to watch, and free good music as well that you can play on your other devices free of charge. I will gladly renew my Prime subscription, even if I do have to pay for a movie once in a while. Also note, jaded Directv users- Amazon charges much less to watch a new movie. text_fidelity_a:
ASUS C100PA-DB02 10.1-inch Touch Chromebook Flip (1.8GHz, 4GB Memory, 16GB eMMC, Google OS), All Metal Body When my dog chewed up the cord to my 2012 Samsung Chromebook, instead of getting a new cord, I decided maybe it was time to get a new Chromebook. After reading all the "top five" reviews I could find, I decided to get this ASUS Chromebook Flip because of the excellent build quality compared to the others and the features. My partner has a Windows-based ASUS tablet this same size that he has really loved, so I knew the ASUS brand would be dependable. However, I didn't realize that this one would be the same size as his, but had I been thinking clearly I would have realized I would not be happy with the smaller keyboard size.

When the Flip came, I was definitely impressed with its build. Everything the reviewers said was true. I was thinking about sending it back, but then DP mentioned that he wished he had an ASUS like the Flip that could run Linux; apparently, he's going to sell his other ASUS because he's quitting Windows and the other ASUS machine has something proprietary about it that prevents him from being able to install Linux on it. Other than that, he loves it. He said he didn't want a Chromebook. But I searched and discovered that Linux CAN be put on the Flip and told him so, so he happily took it. I don't think he realized, either, how great a Chromebook is when you're cloud-centric like I am, and like he's increasingly becoming, so he casually mentioned to me last night that he might not even put Linux on it. There's no reason why he couldn't boot Linux from a flash drive, I don't think, if he wants to leave the Chrome as the main system OS.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS C100PA-DB02 10.1-inch Touch Chromebook Flip (1.8GHz, 4GB Memory, 16GB eMMC, Google OS), All Metal Body

Acer CB273U bemipruzx 27" WQHD 2560 x 1440 IPS Professional Docking Monitor with AMD FreeSync | Delta E<1 | 99% sRGB | HDR10 | TUV/Eyesafe | Display Port, HDMI 2.0, USB Type-C, Ethernet & USB Ports UPDATE: Despite the manual not offering any solution that worked for a dead monitor (no display, no power indicator light) I managed to bring it back to life! With the power switched on I held the three buttons in the back + the nipple down for several seconds, until maybe 15 seconds later the monitor lit up once more and I got an amber power indicator light. What a relief, I really didn't want to wait for a replacement!

This display produces beautiful and accurate colors once you turn down the brightness significantly, which I set to 30. The contrast is good but nothing to write home about.

I use this primarily for gaming, so the first thing I did was enable GSync from nvidia control panel, and set a framerate limiter of 72 using rivatuner (3 less than the 75hz refresh rate of the monitor, as is recommended). And I am really impressed, motion is fluid and responsive like I've never seen before as I'm coming from a 60hz TN panel, significantly better than just Vsync on that. Works perfectly on every game I've tried on it, including Far Cry 5, GTA, Modern Warfare, The Witcher 3, Shadow of the Tomb Raider, FIFA etc. I would have gone for a 144hz display but given the capabilities of my 1070ti for the games I play, 75hz seemed like the sweet spot for me. Highly recommended

Original review* DOA. Worked for 10 mins or so, then simply turned off while I was tweaking picture settings on its OSD. Tried swapping the power cable, flipped the switch and waited a few seconds but nothing, no power indicator light at all.

I feel like giving this model another shot, will update once received.*
text_fidelity_b: Acer CB273U bemipruzx 27" WQHD 2560 x 1440 IPS Professional Docking Monitor with AMD FreeSync | Delta E<1 | 99% sRGB | HDR10 | TUV/Eyesafe | Display Port, HDMI 2.0, USB Type-C, Ethernet & USB Ports

Logitech G240 Cloth Gaming Mouse Pad for Low-DPI Gaming I'm not a gamer. I wanted to try this mouse pad out for graphics (photo editing, vector graphics, and so forth). I'm not a big fan of pen-type tablet input devices. I've always preferred working with a mouse. (To me, the only real down side to using a mouse instead of a tablet input is loss of pressure sensitivity, but there are plenty of workarounds.)

This pad works great. An optical/laser mouse reads it very well, with the slightest movements picked up. The bottom of the pad is grippy enough for the pad to stay put, and the surface, while satin-like, still has enough resistance to provide a lot of fine control.

It's also larger than I expected. It's 11 inches by 13.5 inches. And it is quite flexible and rolls up easily for storage or transport.

Here are some tips for getting precise mouse control:

First of all understand that a low-DPI setting means your pointer doesn't move far when you move the mouse. This enables gamers to aim and target precisely in-game. It also enables artists to precisely move the pointers when working on graphics. How far your cursor/pointer moves is entirely up to you and can be adjusted in your control panel for pointer settings (or, depending on the game, possibly can be adjusted in your game settings).

In that control panel, uncheck "enhance pointer precision." This will turn off pointer acceleration, which can adversely affect control. If the software (or game) you're using overrides this (rare in graphics software, but more common in games), you may have to employ a fix. Just do a search for "Windows 7/8 mouse fix" and you'll find plenty of information on how to do this.

Anyway, it's a great pad for precision cursor control with a mouse, whether for gaming or graphics.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech G240 Cloth Gaming Mouse Pad for Low-DPI Gaming

Kindle Oasis E-reader with Leather Charging Cover - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity, Built-In Audible (Previous Generation - 8th) I've been an avid fan of ebooks since the long gone days of the Rocket and the eBookman, and a fan of the Kindle since the very beginning. This is miles and away the best there has ever been. It is a luxury model, no doubt, but oh is it luxurious.

I like:
The weight. Even in the case it's very light, though if it gets much lighter I'll worry about it blowing away in a strong wind.
The size. It's not going to get much smaller without shrinking the screen.
The interface. I'm sorry, I like buttons. Call me old. I never bent back the spine of a book (horrors) so I can't compare the feel of this to that, but I can say it's nice for a long reading session. The touch screen takes a bit of getting used to, but the tutorial will guide a new user. The tutorial is intrusive at first, but provides useful information and goes away quickly. I will suggest customizing the screen. I hated the default, but you get a lot of options to make it just the way you want.
The lighting is now all but invisible. I was unhappy that you can't completely turn it off as you could with the Nook Glowlight, and turning it down casts an odd yellow light over the page, but it's so even now as to be so unintrusive I barely notice going from sunlight to tunnel on the bus home. With the Nook I'd be thrown out of the book to go turn on the light. With the Kindle, I can keep reading without a pause. It does not have adaptive lighting, but I'm not sure it needs it.
The download speed. I don't know if it's supposed to be faster than the Kindle Keyboard (the last one I had with 3G) but it certainly seems that way.
The battery life. Maybe with this thing going for months we'll finally hear an end to the "but my dead tree doesn't run out of power" nonsense.
Next in series. When you're almost done with a book, it tells you where the story continues. Now the next feature I want, and if it does this I haven't seen it yet, is an alert when the next book in a series I'm following is published. Yes, FictFact is great, but I'm greedy and want it right on the device.

I don't like:
It's not waterproof. There was a lot of hope it would be after the Nook went that route.
It's not solar, yet, but there are rumors of a solar cover coming soon.
It doesn't support Audible and the excellent immersive reading between ebook and audiobook. I have a weird love of that feature, seeing what changed print to audio.
Recommended Content and Reading Lists. I shut this feature off. The information seems scattered at best and gave me no useful information, especially considering how precious screen real estate is.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Oasis E-reader with Leather Charging Cover - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity, Built-In Audible (Previous Generation - 8th)
